question: What is the primary visual difference between a standard X-ray and a CT scan image?

options.A: A standard X-ray uses magnetic fields instead of radiation
options.B: A standard X-ray provides three-dimensional moving video
options.C: A CT scan produces cross-sectional slices of body tissues
options.D: A CT scan only images the skeletal system in color

explanation: CT technology reconstructs multiple X-ray angles into detailed cross-sectional slices, whereas a standard X-ray produces a single flat projection. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why do dense structures like bone appear white on a CT monitor?

options.A: Dense tissues absorb high amounts of radiation
options.B: The computer highlights bone using artificial blue dyes
options.C: Dense tissues allow all radiation to pass straight through
options.D: Bone actively emits fluorescent light during the scan

explanation: Radiation attenuation causes dense structures to absorb more of the X-ray beam, reducing the radiation reaching the detectors and rendering them white. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of using contrast media during a CT scan?

options.A: To replace the need for an X-ray tube inside the gantry
options.B: To enhance the visibility of specific tissues and blood vessels
options.C: To completely block all radiation from reaching the patient
options.D: To speed up the physical movement of the scanner table

explanation: Contrast media alters radiation absorption, making target organs, blood vessels, and abnormal lesions much easier to identify. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h2)

question: When would a nurse expect oral contrast to be administered for a CT scan?

options.A: To highlight the deep blood vessels in the brain
options.B: To clearly outline the stomach and bowel loops
options.C: To visualize the interior chambers of the heart muscle
options.D: To check for fractures in the long bones of the leg

explanation: Oral contrast fills the gastrointestinal tract so nurses and radiologists can easily distinguish the bowel from surrounding abdominal organs. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h2)

question: Which medical condition is most commonly evaluated emergently using a head CT scan?
explanation: A head CT is the primary diagnostic tool used to quickly rule out or confirm bleeding inside the skull following trauma or stroke symptoms. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h3)

question: A patient with sudden chest pain and shortness of breath is sent for a specialized CT scan to check for which condition?
explanation: CT pulmonary angiography is specifically utilized to visualize blood flow within the pulmonary arteries and detect blood clots. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h3)

question: Why must a nurse check serum creatinine levels before a contrast-enhanced CT scan?

options.A: To measure the body's ability to absorb oral contrast
options.B: To check for underlying systemic bacterial infections
options.C: To determine the correct amount of radiation dose required
options.D: To evaluate kidney function for clearing the contrast dye

explanation: Iodinated contrast is excreted through the kidneys, so baseline renal function must be known to prevent contrast-induced kidney injury. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h4)

question: Which medication is commonly held following an intravenous contrast procedure to prevent lactic acidosis?
explanation: Metformin is withheld if kidney function temporarily declines after contrast administration to avoid a dangerous buildup of acid in the blood. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the primary reason a patient must remain completely still during a CT scan?

options.A: To prevent motion artifact from blurring the images
options.B: To keep the intravenous contrast line from falling out
options.C: To stop the X-ray tube from overheating inside the gantry
options.D: To reduce the total amount of radiation absorbed by skin

explanation: Movement creates motion artifacts that distort the cross-sectional images, rendering them difficult for the radiologist to interpret accurately. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h5)

question: What normal physical sensation should a nurse warn a patient about when intravenous contrast is injected?

options.A: Severe muscle cramps in the lower extremities
options.B: A sharp burning pain directly in the chest
options.C: A sudden metallic taste and warm flushing feeling
options.D: Sudden numbness and tingling in both hands

explanation: A transient metallic taste and a warm flush spreading through the body are common, harmless side effects of intravenous contrast administration. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is a primary post-procedural nursing intervention after a CT scan with contrast?

options.A: Encouraging high fluid intake to flush out the contrast
options.B: Placing the patient on a clear liquid diet for a full day
options.C: Administering a high dose of intravenous diuretic medication
options.D: Keeping the patient on strict bed rest for twelve hours

explanation: Abundant fluids help the kidneys rapidly excrete the contrast medium, reducing the risk of renal complications. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h6)

question: Which symptom observed hours after a CT scan indicates a delayed allergic reaction to contrast?
explanation: Delayed hypersensitivity reactions can occur hours or even days later, presenting commonly as pruritus, rash, or urticaria. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why is the use of CT scans carefully justified by healthcare providers despite their diagnostic benefits?

options.A: Patients cannot tolerate more than one scan per calendar year
options.B: The contrast dye causes permanent kidney failure in all clients
options.C: Each scan exposes the patient to cumulative ionizing radiation
options.D: CT scanners are extremely expensive to maintain in hospitals

explanation: Ionizing radiation carries a small but real cumulative risk of cellular damage, necessitating careful clinical justification for every scan. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h7)

question: What immediate medication is required if a patient experiences severe anaphylaxis from contrast media?
explanation: Severe allergic anaphylactic reactions compromise the airway and circulation, making epinephrine the primary life-saving emergency drug. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h7)
